applies_to: Shinko PCB1 programmable controllers with the C5W or C5 RS-485 option, native PCB1 command set; manual No. PCB1CE3.
summary: The PCB1 is a ramp/soak program controller with 10 patterns of 10 steps, 10 PID blocks and three event outputs. On RS-485 it speaks Shinko protocol or Modbus ASCII/RTU; every item is a signed 16-bit holding register. The map covers all pattern, event, wait and PID-block items, engineering settings, run/hold/advance commands and the read-only monitor block.

addressing.note: Data items are hex (9000H) and are sent unchanged as the Modbus holding-register address. The manual says the Modicon number is the data item plus 40001. The RTU examples read PV at 9000H and write pattern 1 step 1 SV at 2100H (CRCs A90AH and 83E1H checked).

source.title: Communication Instruction Manual PCB1 (C5W, C5)
source.pages: Command table pp. 24-37; data notes p. 44; communication settings pp. 4-5

notes: Addresses with a pattern or block number follow the manual's digit scheme: 2p00H (pattern p = 1-A), 3p00H, 5p00H, and 4k12H-4k16H for PID block k = 1-A. Step n of a pattern uses 2p00H + (n-1) x 3.
The manual's PCD-33A compatible command set (section 7.2, 0001H-00A3H) is not repeated here; see the pcd-33a map for that layout.
All data are 16-bit two's complement; values with a decimal point are sent as whole numbers.
Units of PID times and limits are not printed in the command table.
Changing an EV allocation clears that event's alarm value-0, hysteresis, delay and energized settings.

integration.summary: Select MODBUS RTU mode in Engineering setting mode 1 and give the unit a non-zero instrument number; then poll PV 9000H, current step SV 9003H, pattern/step 9005H and status 900AH-900BH, and start/stop with 8001H.
integration.enable: Requires the C5W or C5 option. In Engineering setting mode 1 (down + MODE for about 3 s) set Communication protocol to MODBUS RTU (or ASCII), then instrument number, speed, data bit/parity and stop bit. These can only be set on the keypad.
quirks: The manual's Modicon example writes 2100H as 42101, treating the hex digits as decimal; its example frames send 2100H itself as the PDU address (CRCs check), so use the hex data item directly.
Instrument number 0 is the Modbus broadcast address; give each unit 1-95.
The USB console cable and RS-485 cannot be used at the same time.
setup: Factory defaults: Shinko protocol, instrument number 0, 9600 bps, 7 bits/even parity, 1 stop bit, 10 ms response delay.
For Modbus RTU choose an 8-bit data format (8 bits/no, even or odd parity).
Do not fit a terminator; the unit has built-in pull-up/pull-down resistors.
gotchas: HOLD and ADVANCE return exception 17 (11H) while the program is stopped.
Exception 18 (12H) is returned while the keypad is in setting mode.
Non-volatile memory takes about one million writes; avoid cyclic writes of settings.
